The '''Premier League Golden Boot''' is an annual [[association football]] award presented to the leading goalscorer in the [[Premier League]]. For sponsorship purposes, it was called the [[Carling]] Golden Boot from 1994 to 2001, the [[Barclaycard]] Golden Boot from 2002 to 2004, the [[Barclays]] Golden Boot from 2005 to 2016, the [[Cadbury]] Golden Boot from 2017 to 2020,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.premierleague.com/fapl.rac?command=forwardOnly&nextPage=enSeasons |title=Premier League Awards |publisher=Premier League |access-date=1 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061210142537/http://www.premierleague.com/fapl.rac?command=forwardOnly&nextPage=enSeasons |archive-date=10 December 2006 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=history>{{cite web|title=History of the Premier League |url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/about/history.html |publisher=Premier League |access-date=1 January 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120421110805/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/about/history.html |archive-date=21 April 2012 }}</ref>, the [[Coca-Cola Zero Sugar]] Golden Boot for 2021, the [[Castrol]] Golden Boot from 2022 to 2024 and the [[Premier League]] Golden Boot in 2025. Since 2026, it is referred to as the [[Coca-Cola]] Golden Boot. In addition to the trophy, winners of the Golden Boot are usually given [[Pound sterling|£]]1,000 for every goal they scored throughout the season to donate to a charity of their choice,<ref name=ronaldo>{{cite news |title=Ronaldo & Ferguson win top awards |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/7401795.stm |work=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=14 May 2008 |access-date=3 January 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Van Nistelrooy has final say |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2404029/Van-Nistelrooy-has-final-say.html |date=14 May 2003 |access-date=1 January 2014 |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph }}</ref> although [[Robin van Persie]] was given £30,000 after scoring 26 goals in the [[2012–13 Premier League|2012–13 season]].<ref name=retains/><ref>{{cite news|title=Van Persie picks up Premier League Golden Boot|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/2896/premier-league/2013/05/22/3996508/van-persie-picks-up-premier-league-golden-boot|date=22 May 2013|access-date=15 January 2014|first=Joe|last=Doyle|work=Goal.com|publisher=Perform Group}}</ref>

The Premier League was founded in 1992, when the clubs of the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] left [[English Football League|the Football League]] and established a new commercially independent league that negotiated its own broadcast and sponsorship agreements.<ref name=history/> The newly formed league had no [[Sponsor (commercial)|sponsor]] for its [[1992–93 FA Premier League|inaugural season]] until Carling agreed to a four-year £12&nbsp;million deal that started the [[1993–94 FA Premier League|following season]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/1118425.stm |title=Why Carling called time on Premiership |first=Peter |last=Jones |date=19 January 2001 |work=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|access-date=1 January 2014 }}</ref> and it was simply known as the Premier League in its first year.<ref name=history/> As a result, the award was called the "Premier League Golden Boot" when [[Teddy Sheringham]] received the inaugural award in 1993.<ref name=top/> Originally consisting of 22 teams, the league contracted to 20 teams after the [[1994–95 FA Premier League|1994–95 season]]; this reduced the number of games played from 42 to 38.<ref name=history/>

[[Thierry Henry]] and [[Mohamed Salah]] have both won the Golden Boot on four occasions, more than any other player. [[Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink]] and [[Dwight Yorke]] were the first [[List of foreign Premier League players|non-English and non-European]] winners, respectively, when they shared the award with [[Michael Owen]] in 1999.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dpvNY8B_2XAC&q=dwight+yorke+overseas+player+golden+boot&pg=PT17|title=Kissing the Badge: How much do you know about 20 years of the Premier League?|publisher=A & C Black|date=7 May 2012|editor-last=Ascough|editor-first=Phil|access-date=4 January 2014|isbn=9781408178539}}</ref> [[Alan Shearer]] and Henry have won the award in three consecutive seasons.<ref name=break>{{cite news|title=Will Luis Suarez break the Premier League goal scoring record this season?|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/will-luis-suarez-break-the-premier-league-goal-scoring-record-this-season-29861426.html|date=23 December 2013|access-date=4 January 2014|first=Declan|last=Whooley|newspaper=Irish Independent}}</ref> [[Kevin Phillips (English footballer)|Kevin Phillips]], Henry, [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] and [[Erling Haaland]] won the [[European Golden Shoe]] in the same season as the Premier League Golden Boot,<ref name=break/><ref name=Madeira>{{cite news |title=Ronaldo receives Golden Boot in his native Madeira |url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-ronaldo-boot-idUKLD30291020080913 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190512161542/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-ronaldo-boot-idUKLD30291020080913 |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 May 2019 |date=14 September 2008 |access-date=7 October 2013 |first=Carlos |last=Pontes |publisher=Reuters}}</ref> with Henry achieving this on two occasions (2004 and 2005).<ref name=fits>{{cite news |title=Golden Shoe fits for Thierry Henry |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/golden-shoe-fits-for-thierry-henry |date=31 May 2005 |access-date=7 October 2013 |work=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal FC |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203012653/http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/golden-shoe-fits-for-thierry-henry |archive-date=3 December 2013}}</ref> Shearer, Hasselbaink and Van Persie are the only players to win the Golden Boot with two clubs.<ref>{{cite news|title=Premier League 2012–13: the season in numbers|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/may/20/2012-13-premier-league-in-numbers|date=20 May 2013|access-date=5 January 2014|newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref>

Haaland scored the most goals to win the Golden Boot, with 36 in [[2022–23 Premier League|2022–23]].<ref>{{cite news |title=For the record: Premier League facts and figures |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/59886 |publisher=Premier League |date=16 May 2018 |access-date=29 May 2023 }}</ref> With 35 games played in the season, he also recorded the highest goals-to-games ratio to win the award, of 1.03. [[Nicolas Anelka]] scored the fewest goals to clinch the award outright, with 19 goals in [[2008–09 Premier League|2008–09]].<ref name=top/> The all-time record for lowest number of goals scored to be bestowed the award, however, is 18 goals; this was achieved during the [[1997–98 FA Premier League|1997–98]] and [[1998–99 FA Premier League|1998–99]] seasons, when the award was shared between three players both times.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nicolas Anelka Wins Premier League Golden Boot|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/9/england/2009/05/24/1283976/nicolas-anelka-wins-premier-league-golden-boot|date=24 May 2009|access-date=4 January 2014|first=Albert|last=Dumont|work=Goal.com|publisher=Perform Group}}</ref> The latter season marked the last time the Golden Boot was shared until [[2010–11 Premier League|2010–11]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Statistical breakdown of EPL season|url=https://www.espn.com/sports/soccer/blog/_/name/five_aside/id/6577834/statistical-breakdown-premier-league-season-five-aside-soccer|date=23 May 2011|access-date=4 January 2014|first=Paul|last=Carr|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|work=ESPN}}</ref> when [[Dimitar Berbatov]] and [[Carlos Tevez]] both scored 20 goals that season to tie for the award.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dimitar Berbatov's bizarre season|url=https://www.espn.com/sports/soccer/blog/_/name/martin_james/id/6618790/dimitar-berbatov-bizarre-season-manchester-united-soccer|date=2 June 2011|access-date=4 January 2014|first=James|last=Martin|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|work=ESPN}}</ref> Since then, the award was shared two more times: in [[2018–19 Premier League|2018–19]] (by three players) and in [[2021–22 Premier League|2021–22]] (two players). Notably, [[Son Heung-min]], who shared the award with Salah in the 2021–22 season, became the first Asian player to win the Golden Boot.<ref>{{cite news |date=22 May 2022 |title=Son and Salah win 2021/22 Golden Boot award |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/2626553 |access-date=7 September 2025 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref> Erling Haaland holds the Premier League Golden Boot after scoring 27 goals in [[2025–26 Premier League|2025–26]]. It was his third, putting him level with Harry Kane and Alan Shearer.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-24 |title=Haaland wins 2025/26 Premier League Golden Boot award |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4591856/haaland-wins-202526-premier-league-golden-boot-award |access-date=2026-10-18 |website=www.premierleague.com |language=en}}</ref>
